items.body: Two developments moved the tape yesterday and this morning.
items.lede: Two developments moved the tape yesterday and this morning. First, CBP disclosed in a CIT status filing Tuesday that cumulative IEEPA refunds have crossed $100 billion — roughly 60% of the ~$166 billion collected — a meaningful throughput milestone that nevertheless leaves the hardest categories of claims still in queue and the DOJ's Federal Circuit appeal of the underlying refund order fully live. Second, 25 Democratic-led states filed a new CIT complaint Monday challenging the Section 301 forced-labor tariffs that went live on July 24, adding a third front to litigation that is already testing the outer limits of executive tariff authority. Both developments have direct implications for the refund math and for the new-tariff exposure that importers are now carrying.

The material development of the past two weeks — final approval of Bartz — remains the controlling posture across this desk, and the next hard milestone of consequence is the October 21, 2026 summary-judgment hearing in Concord I. What follows is a calibrated carry-forward for both key-focus matters, plus the parallel-docket signals that bear on recovery posture and fair-use framework development.

items.lede: Two significant developments broke Monday through Tuesday: the free-fall Chapter 11 petition of Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation and eleven affiliated debtors in the Southern District of Texas — the largest new mega-case filing in this cycle — and the filing of a $15 million settlement term sheet in the long-running Jackson Walker / Judge David Jones ethics litigation, also in the Southern District of Texas. The Kahan appeal (Bankr. D. Mass., No. 24-11592) logged a statement of issues and record designation on August 3, signaling that appellate briefing is now formally opened. BlockFills (Bankr. D. Del., No. 26-10371) filed a Certificate of Service on August 4 — administrative only, no substantive movement.
